6.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     6.1   BYLAW NO. 2009

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2009 at 6:13 pm.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew Moradian has applied on
           behalf of Langford Central Developments Inc. to amend the zoning of 2739 to 2751
           Scafe Road and 2746 Peatt Road from the 'One-and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the
           'City Centre Pedestrian' Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of 2 mixed-used buildings
that would be 18 and 24 storeys in height.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
contributions prior to issuance of a building permit:
1.   $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
2.   $2,850 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
subject to reductions depending on use and height in accordance with the Affordable
Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

The applicant will also provide $10.75 per square metre of commercial space towards
the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to issuance of a building permit.

That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
agrees to the following:

1. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan, and a
construction parking plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of building permit.
2. That all 6 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated prior to issuance
of a Development Permit.
3. That onsite parking is allocated to each unit in accordance with the zoning bylaw.
4. That a strata plan is registered for each building prior to issuance of an occupancy
permit.
5. That 100% of the residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging
for electric vehicles.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'City Centre' designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom provided a presentation on the proposed
    development on behalf of the applicant. The project would provide housing for 271
    families and commercial space in the centre of Langford, and is not requesting any
    variances. The project will be using carbon reduction technology in its concrete.
    Prices for homes will start under $400K.

•   Liisa Stewart - 2723 Peatt Road - Do not feel this development is reasonable for the
    neighbourhood. Have been negatively impacted by a four-storey development
    nearby and this would be worse. Support development of 4-6 stories.

•   Ryan Craycroft - 738 Walfred Road - Have 100+ employees, many of whom will not
    be able to get into the market without developments like this. Support this
    development, will house young families.

    Michael Biscoe - 2958 Sea Point Drive - Support this project.

    Resident - Willshire Drive - Some people are not able to find housing in Langford
    and have to commute.

    Matthew McKay- 780 Hockley Avenue - Support this development, support the job
    development and economic development created by this development. Many
    rental properties have a zero vacancy. We need more developments like this.
    People who live in dense areas are often able to walk to work and don't negatively
    impact traffic.

    Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Request that Council vote no to tall
    towers, which will set a negative precedent and compound existing traffic, parking,
    services, and infrastructure issues. There was not sufficient community consultation
    on this development or on the zoning bylaw that allowed developments of this
    height. Prefer a staged approach to development.

    Mary Wagner - 103-2669 Deville Road - Clarified that the carbon sequestering
    technology will be used in the concrete for this development. Do not support zones
    with no height limit, feel that the OCP needs more community input. Request more
    green space, would like the neighbourhood to be walkable.

•   David Fulko, 3035 Dorado Court - In favour of this development. Housing is needed
    right now, and it is better to go up than out, environmentally speaking. It is better
    to have more housing than prioritize traffic. It is appropriate to densify the city core,
    this will add energy, vibrancy, and support arts venues and local businesses. Taller
    buildings often have bigger setbacks and allow more space in the neighbourhood.

•   Anil Karim- Working with the developers to include quality child care within this
    development. The developers strongly support the effort to maximize equitable
    childcare spaces, which serve families who might not have access to quality
    childcare otherwise. Childcare is especially challenging for fast-growing cities, and
    this development is especially appropriate for childcare since it and Langford attract
    young families.

•   Robert Friend, 3024 Glen Lake Road - Employ 50 employees who live and work in
    Langford. Employees are getting pushed out of the city. Taller, dense projects are
    needed to support the growth in the city and families who want to stay in Langford.

•   Resident on 3207 Willshire Drive - Langford is a very fast-growing community. We
    need to house people and labour. People are sharing bedrooms and houses.
    Support this development.

•   Dana Elizabeth - 2850 Aldwynd Road - Support this project and density in the core.
    More homes will help facilitate growth, infrastructure, housing, and walkability.

•   Michael Sikich - 849 Homer Street - Will be marketing this development if it comes
    on the market. Langford is very desirable, which affects affordability. These tall,
    dense developments help address affordability and allow more people to achieve
    home ownership and a sense of pride and community. Taller developments reduce
    urban sprawl and allow more green space around the development.

•   Thai Tran - 2853 Crystal View Drive - Support this project for the affordability that it
    brings. Will set a positive precedent and make the downtown core more livable,
    walkable for young families.

•   Rosemary Turnowski - 837 Brock Avenue - This development would have a huge
    impact. Have worked hard for years to build a sense of community and get to know
    neighbours. Those in favour do not live near the proposed development, and it will
    affect the community. Will affect ability to garden, parking. Feel that this will blow
    up the community.

•   Bryce Wade - 19721 64th Avenue, Langley - Housing crisis requires projects like this.
    Thought he would never be able to afford housing in Vancouver, but working
    remotely will allow this. The only way to provide housing and avoid urban sprawl is
    to build up like this. This project is important for our community and economy.

•   Morgan Petrovic - 309-2717 Peatt Road - Will be impacted by the project since it is
    nearby, but fully support it. Despite potential annoyances, don't think the
    difficulties will be as bad as many believe. Think this will bring jobs for construction,
    local businesses. The centre of communities should grow, and Langford will become
    a bigger city.

•   Jackie Sheridan -1005 Golden Spire Crescent - Concerned about the height of the
    proposal and believe there may be issues with infrastructure for buildings over 6
    stories

              Mayor Young left the meeting at 7:17 pm.

•   Jackie Sheridan -1005 Golden Spire Crescent - believe that these will not allow
    young families to enter the housing market since all housing is unaffordable now.
    These buildings are not eco-friendly.

•   Layne Britton - 3022 Shoreview Drive - Support this project, it is vital for the
    downtown Langford core.

              Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 7:19 pm.

•   Layne Britton continued - Langford has become one of the most desirable places to
    live, and do not think this will negatively impact traffic and parking.

•   Mike, 953 Glen Willow Place - Support this project, this is more environmentally-
    friendly than urban sprawl. High-rise buildings are more energy-efficient than other

•   Nicole Simpson - 4111 Mariposa Heights - Support this development. There is a

•   Susie Hicks -2345 Lake End - Agree with previous callers who have voiced concerns

•   Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfield Terrace - Oppose development. This neighbourhood

•   Jordan Goldsmith - 3030 Washington Avenue - Grew up in Langford and have a lot

    Elizabeth Markus - 3262 Zapata Place - Ask Council to vote against this
    development. Council must do more community engagement to understand the
    vision of residents. Residents may not want Langford to become a more urban city.
    Residents have been left out of the process. This will forever change the character
    of Langford. Do not believe this development is environmentally-friendly. Feel high

    Kim Robinson - 960B Paige Avenue - Agree with everyone who opposes this project.
    Do not agree 24 stories is appropriate for this neighbourhood. 10 stories would be
    more appropriate. Feel that residents will have no say once it is built.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None.

      Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2009 closed at 7:51 p.m.

6.2   BYLAW NO. 2008


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2008 at 7:51 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew Moradian has applied on
      behalf of Langford Gateway Developments to amend the zoning of 2633 to 2647
      Sunderland Road, 808 to 820 Arncote Road, and 2630 to 2646 Peatt Road from the
      'One-and Two-Family Residential' Zone to the 'City Centre Pedestrian' Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of 4 mixed-used buildings
      that would range in height from 13 to 22 storeys.

      As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to the following:

      That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
      contributions prior to issuance of a building permit:
      1. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2. $2,850 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      subject to reductions depending on use and height in accordance with the Affordable
      Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

      The applicant will also provide $10.75 per square metre of commercial space towards
      the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to issuance of a building permit.

      That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
      agrees to the following:

      1. That full frontage improvements, recommendations from the associated Traffic
      Impact Assessment, a storm water management plan, and a construction parking plan
      be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the
      Director of Engineering prior to issuance of building permit.
      2. That all 11 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated prior to
      issuance of a Development Permit.
      3. That onsite parking is allocated to each unit in accordance with the zoning bylaw.
      4. That a strata plan is registered for each building prior to issuance of an occupancy
      permit.
      5. That 100% of the residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging
      for electric vehicles.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'City Centre' designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•   Matthew Moradian and Rachel Sansom on behalf of Langford Gateway
    Developments.

           Councillor Blackwell left the meeting at 7:54 pm.

    for 444 families on just over 2 acres of land and will provide 11 500 square feet of
    commercial and daycare space. Will provide approximately $2.6 million in park and
    amenity contributions and is requesting no variances. Housing 444 families in single
    family homes would require 111 acres of land.

           Councillor Blackwell returned to the meeting at 7:58 pm.

    Anais Holdaway -101-827 Arncote Avenue - Oppose this development. There was

    Yazmin Hernandez - 2634 Sunderland Road - Traffic Impact Assessments will never

           Councillor Wade left the meeting at 8:16 pm.

    Tim Revino -101-1663 MacKenzie Ave - Have planning and density, and know
    people who are currently sharing small units with 5+ roommates and bunkbeds in

           Councillor Wade returned to the meeting at 8:19 pm

•   Matthew McKay - 784 Hockley Avenue - This is an exciting development, could be
    improved by a public plaza and public art. An art walk would be a great addition to

•   Jacqueline Gintaut -1331 Ravensview Drive - Agree with first two callers.

           Councillor Seaton left the meeting at 8:21 pm.

•   Jacqueline Gintaut continued - Request that Council vote no to tall towers, which
    will set a negative precedent and compound existing traffic, parking, services, and
    infrastructure issues. There was not sufficient community consultation on this
    development or on the zoning bylaw that allowed developments of this height.

             Councillor Seaton returned to the meeting at 8:24 pm. Mayor Young left the

•   Mary Wagner -103-2669 Deville Road - Suggest having a significant plaza or corner

•   Michael Biscoe - 2958 Seapoint Drive - Support this development. First time

•   Warren Grey -15195 36th Ave Surrey, BC - Would like to move to Langford, support
    this project.

•   Dana Elizabeth - 2850 Aldwynd Road - Would like to thank Council for supporting
    high density housing. We desperately need more housing options since we are in a
    housing crisis. Support the height and density. Know people who have had to buy in
    Mill Bay, Sooke and Duncan; this will help people stay in Langford.

•   Darlene Oudot - 105-827 Arncote Avenue - Invite Council to come to the

•   Andy Kading - 3257 Doncaster Drive - Represent Watt Consulting Group, which

•   Wendy Hobbs - 3442 Luxton Road - Support the callers who are saying that there

•   Andrew Fox - 2634 Sunderland Road - Question the rosy picture that developers are
    painting. Concerns about number of childcare spots and traffic. The amenities and
    infrastructure aren't present for this development. This will download the burden of

•   Acting Director of Corporate Services Marie Watmough - there will be
    approximately 85 childcare spots

•   Laurie Plomp - 3592 Whimfield Terrace - The density will strongly impact the
    neighbourhood. Council should listen to neighbourhood residents. Although the
    project was initiated in 2019, it was not discussed with local residents until recently

      •   Isaac Mann - 2747 Scafe Road - Support this project. A lot of the issues brought up

      •   Ryan Craycroft - 738 Walfred Road - This development will help address
          infrastructure issues by providing more tax dollars. Support this development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      •   Jason Mackenzie - 996 Cavalcade Terrace - Council should listen to current residents
          and build appropriate density, not necessarily high density. Request that Council
          reject the application.

      •   Acting Director of Corporate Services Marie Watmough - Correction, there is the
          possibility of 300-400 daycare spots.

      Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
      the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2008 closed at 8:52 p.m.

6.3   BYLAW NO. 1992

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1992 at 8:52 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that City of Langford staff have applied
      on behalf of City of Langford to amend the Zoning Bylaw No. 300 by updating the
      definitions for ''suites'' and "kitchens", adding a new definition for "public assembly and
      entertainment use", and refining Part 2 for enforceability purposes. These changes were
      initially left out of the spring omnibus (Bylaw 1944) while City Staff collaborated to
      ensure that Council and Departmental desires were incorporated.

      Bylaw 1992 proposes changes to Zoning Bylaw No. 300 Part 1 Definitions and Part 2
      General Provisions to allow for increased usability, education and enforcement of the
      Zoning Bylaw No. 300 for City Staff and the general public.

      As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

6.4   BYLAW NO. 1931


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1931 at 8:53 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that The City of Langford has applied to
annend the zoning of 1365 Goldstreann Avenue from the AM (Amenity) Zone to Area 5 -
Multi-Family of the CDl (Comprehensive Development 1 - Goldstream Meadows) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a 6-storey multi-family
building.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
regulations of the Local Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
contributions per residential unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:
a) $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b) $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
a) That parking stalls are allocated to individual units and visitors as required by the
Zoning Bylaw;
b) That a strata plan of the building is registered prior to occupancy;
c) That residential parking stalls are provided with Level 2 charging capabilities;
d) That the following are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of
the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:
i. Frontage improvements;
ii. A storm water management plan; and
iii. A construction parking and traffic management plan;

The applicant has provided a stormwater management memo, to the satisfaction of the
Director of Engineering, as required by Council.

The applicant has furthermore committed to providing 30% of the units in the proposed
development for sale through the City's new Attainable Home Ownership Program.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Mixed Use Employment
Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

      contributions per single-family dwelling prior to subdivision:
      1.   $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2.   $6,000 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      That as a bonus for increased density, the applicant will provide the following
      contributions per townhouse dwelling prior to building permit:


1. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
2. $3,660 toward the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

That prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will register a section 219 covenant that
agrees to the following:
1. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan, and a
construction parking plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to subdivision approval for the single-
family dwellings, or prior to building permit for the townhouse dwellings.
2. That 0.387 hectares of land immediately west of the single-family lots be dedicated
as Park at the time of subdivision.
3.   That a Statutory Right of Way be registered on the townhouse site to allow the City
access to the future Park.
4. That an easement for a sewer force main be registered over the single-family side of
development, in favour of the townhouse side.
5. That the townhomes abutting the rear property lines of 3413-3425 Luxton Road be
limited in height to 2-storeys.
6. That a playground area, approximately 320m^ in size be provided within the
townhouse side of development.
7. That the full amount of General Amenity Contribution from the townhouse side be
secured prior to issuance of the first building permit and used to complete the sidewalk
along the eastern side of Luxton Road north of this site.
8. That future home owners are notified of the potential nuisances that may arise
from surround land uses, specially those uses related to agriculture and from that South
Vancouver Island Rangers gun range.
9. That future home owners are notified that garages are to be used for off-street
parking and not storage that prevents parking.
This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan 'Neighbourhood'
designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.



The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

•    Ron Coutre - 205-847 Goldstream Avenue - There is a housing crisis. This is a family-
     oriented townhome project that will include a full environmental assessment. While
     residents may prefer no development at all, most seemed amenable to the type of
     development proposed, and at least one resident supports it.

•    Matthew McKay - 784 Hockley Avenue - Support this development, appreciate the
     greenery and separation between units.

•    George Weatherall - 925 Latoria Road - Fully support this project, think it would be a
     nice addition to the area.

•    Morgan Petrovic - 309-2717 Peatt Road - Fully support this rezoning. The developer
     has found a good balance between good homes and an affordable development.
     There is decent greenspace and all of the issues that have come up have been
     addressed.


           •   Chris Tysol - 2934 Robalee Place - Rent in Langford and would like to purchase.
               Developments like this are a good opportunity to get into the market.

           •   Wendy Hobbs - 3442 Luxton Road - Not speaking against the development, but have
               concerns that it is in a 200-year floodplain. Hope that the City will ensure this will be
               built to withstand flooding. Do not support density on a floodplain. Traffic on Luxton
               Road is already busy with pedestrian traffic. Request that the sidewalk will be
               extended. Concerned that there will be a covenant that residents cannot complain
               about existing uses, and that there is not adequate fire service on that side of
               Langford.

           •   Brody Coulter -1121 Lipincott Road - Support this project, happy to have more
               family-friendly housing.

                      Mayor Young left the meeting at 9:52 pm.

           •   Michael Harris - 953 Glen Willow Place - Fully support this development.

           •   Steve Webber - 3437 Luxton Road - Concerned about flooding. Luxton Road was
               closed on Monday due to flooding from Firehall Creek.

                      Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 9:54 pm.

           •   Steve Webber continued - Request that there be a plan to address flooding. Would
               like there to be one less townhouse, and more parking added.

           •   Colby Messer - 2149 Triangle Trail - Support this development, appreciate the
               greenspace in the plan. Feel it would improve what's there now.

           Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

           Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared
           the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2004 closed at 9:56 p.m.
